gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Noto Sans Osmanya has wide, easy s curves and a lowercase that towers over its own capitals. Tektur sits above it with open-ended curves and wire-thin outlines, and the two would carry a long page without tiring the eye.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hmong: Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong sets a high x-height and rounds that gap open like a cracked bangle, under a heading with outsized lowercase. Tektur's spine matches its terminals.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-palmyrene: Tektur's pipe-cleaner strokes never swell or thin, and every curve is left generously open at its ends. Noto Sans Palmyrene follows with compressed ascenders and curves that stop short, a quieter sans-serif partner on the same page.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-hau: Tektur draws its outsized lowercase in a plain, unshaded line that never swells, with every curve left open at the end. Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau answers in a sans with room inside its curves and capitals that barely top the lowercase.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Noto Sans PhagsPa is a friendly sans-serif with see-through c openings and a gentle bump up to its capitals. Tektur is the showier one, looking nib-drawn at a fixed width.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-phoenician: Noto Sans Phoenician has generous lowercase height and s curves that open wide at both ends. Tektur brings rope-thick curves and outsized lowercase, while Noto Sans Phoenician keeps the page open and modern in its sans manner.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-psalter-pahla: Approachable describes Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi, with its gaping e mouths and capitals that barely rise above the lowercase. Tektur adds a steady, marker-like line and oversized lowercase, and its display swagger is the pair's best asset.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Noto Sans Rejang has lowercase counters like wide glass portholes and clear gaps in c, e, s and a. Tektur draws its outsized letters with wire-thick strokes, and that wiry display voice beside the open sans is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-runic: Noto Sans Runic has a big x-height and curves that never close on themselves. Tektur lays flat, single-weight linework above it, and the heading's outsized lowercase and open terminals give the page two clearly different voices.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Tektur's pipe-cleaner strokes carry no thick-thin swell, as a pointed brush would give, and every curve ends open. Noto Sans Samaritan, a hefty sans-serif with daylight inside its curves, would read comfortably down a page.
